description: Novelty pruning keeps only the states of a search that bring something new. Each state is described by integer *features*, such as the facts that hold in it. The *novelty* of a state is the size of the smallest set of its features that no earlier state had all at once; if every set of up to `k` features was seen before, the novelty counts as greater than `k`. A `NoveltyTable` records every feature set of size up to `k` that it has seen, so with `n` features it holds at most `O(n^k)` sets. IW and SIW drop each non-goal state with novelty above `k`, so they need no heuristic. BFWS keeps such states and uses novelty as its first sort key.
